title: Integral Formula for an Independent Affine Input
statement: Let $(\Omega,\mu)$ be a probability space, and let $A,D,W\colon\Omega\to\mathbb R$ be measurable up to null sets, with $W$ independent of the pair $(A,D)$. If $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\psi(A+DW)$ is integrable, then the function $q(a,d)=\mathbb E[\psi(a+dW)]$ is integrable under the distribution of $(A,D)$, and $\mathbb E[\psi(A+DW)]=\int_{\mathbb R^2}q(a,d)\,d\mathcal L(A,D)(a,d)$.
hypotheses_covered: $(A,D)$ is measurable up to null sets
$W$ is measurable up to null sets
replaced: Let $A,D,W$ be real functions on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$ such that $(A,D)$ and $W$ are measurable up to null sets and $W$ is independent of $(A,D)$. If $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\psi(A+DW)$ is integrable, then $q(a,d)=\mathbb E_\mu[\psi(a+dW)]$ is integrable under the law $\lambda$ of $(A,D)$ and $\mathbb E_\mu[\psi(A+DW)]=\int q(a,d)\,d\lambda(a,d)$.
